chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Ismāʿīl al-Juʿfī, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him, 'A man divorced his wife.' He said, 'He has more right to take her back (during the waiting period) as long as she has not passed the blood of the third menstruation.'

key_terms.الطَّلَاق: Divorce; the legal dissolution or suspension of marriage.
key_terms.الْحَيْضَة: Menstruation; the monthly bleeding cycle used to calculate the waiting period.
key_terms.رَجْعَة: Right of revocation; the husband's right to take back his divorced wife during the waiting period without a new contract.

ai.seo_question: When does a revocable divorce become final in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Tahdhib clarifies the specific condition for the finality of a revocable divorce (ṭalāq rajʿī), establishing that the husband's right to take his wife back persists until the third menstrual cycle is fully completed. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the physical completion of the ʿiddah period as the definitive marker for the transition to an irrevocable state, ensuring clarity in marital status before any potential remarriage or new waiting period.
